key_insight: The paper identifies goal grounding—not exploration—as the main weakness of navigation policies built from pretrained vision-language models. These policies often miss a target already in view or misjudge its distance.
problem_solved: Object-goal navigation policies can explore effectively yet still fail to reach a requested object because they do not reliably recognize and locate it in their current view.
method: Diagnose failures in navigation policies fine-tuned from pretrained vision-language models.
Focus on two goal-grounding capabilities: noticing visible target objects and estimating their distance.
The supplied abstract is truncated before the proposed StopWatch mechanism is described, so implementation details cannot be summarized reliably.
impact: The findings suggest that practitioners should evaluate target recognition and distance estimation separately from exploration. Improving these capabilities may offer a more focused route to better navigation success.
visual_elements: Split-panel scene: a robot explores successfully but overlooks the requested object already in view.
Navigation pipeline highlighting goal recognition and distance estimation as bottlenecks.
Robot-camera view with a target bounding box and a robot-to-object distance marker.
Conceptual comparison of exploration failures versus goal-grounding failures, without invented numerical results.
paper_title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
paper_authors: Xinhao Liu, Yunsheng Tian, Yuheng Qiu, Pieter Abbeel, Xi Chen
